_meta.indication: Treatment of postmenopausal women with osteoporosis at high risk for fracture (history of osteoporotic fracture, multiple risk factors for fracture, or patients who have failed or are intolerant to other available osteoporosis therapy); reduces the risk of vertebral and nonvertebral fractures.

pivotal_trials.design: 18-month, randomized, multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, with an open-label teriparatide (Forteo) active control arm; abaloparatide 80 mcg or placebo given subcutaneously once daily.
pivotal_trials.population: Postmenopausal women with osteoporosis aged 49 to 86 years (mean age 69); at baseline 24% had at least one prevalent vertebral fracture and 48% had at least one prior nonvertebral fracture.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint: incidence of new (incident) morphometric vertebral fractures at Month 18 in TYMLOS vs placebo.
pivotal_trials.n: N=2463 women with PMO in the phase 3 study; the double-blind primary comparison was TYMLOS (N=824) vs placebo (N=821).
pivotal_trials.result: New vertebral fractures at 18 months: 0.6% TYMLOS vs 4.2% placebo (p<0.0001); absolute risk reduction 3.6%, relative risk reduction 86%. Nonvertebral fractures (18 months + 1 month follow-up): 2.7% TYMLOS vs 4.7% placebo, relative risk reduction 43% (logrank p=0.049).

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence >=2%): hypercalciuria, dizziness, nausea, headache, palpitations, fatigue, upper abdominal pain and vertigo. In Study 003, rates (TYMLOS vs placebo): hypercalciuria 11% vs 9%, dizziness 10% vs 6%, nausea 8% vs 3%, headache 8% vs 6%, palpitations 5% vs 0.4%. Warnings include orthostatic hypotension, hypercalcemia (3% vs 0.1%) and hypercalciuria/urolithiasis.
target_moa: Abaloparatide is a synthetic 34-amino acid analog of parathyroid hormone-related peptide [PTHrP(1-34)] that acts as an agonist at the PTH1 receptor (PTH1R), activating the cAMP signaling pathway; when administered intermittently it has an anabolic effect on bone, increasing bone mass and strength.

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: RISK OF OSTEOSARCOMA. Abaloparatide caused a dose-dependent increase in the incidence of osteosarcoma (a malignant bone tumor) in male and female rats at systemic exposures 4 to 28 times the human 80 mcg exposure; it is unknown if TYMLOS will cause osteosarcoma in humans. Cumulative use of TYMLOS and parathyroid hormone analogs (e.g., teriparatide) for more than 2 years during a patient's lifetime is not recommended.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was convened; FDA did not identify efficacy or safety issues requiring input from an advisory panel.

summary.text: TYMLOS was reviewed as a new molecular entity under PDUFA V ('the Program') because the application contained a new molecular entity received after October 1, 2012; the PDUFA goal date was extended three months for review of additional immunogenicity data. No advisory committee was convened. Two prior requests for Breakthrough Therapy Designation were denied. Approval was traditional (full) approval based on Study 003; the boxed warning for osteosarcoma risk was required with enhanced post-marketing pharmacovigilance of osteosarcoma cases.

citations.quote: This NDA was reviewed under the Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA) V “Program” because it contains a new molecular entity and was received after October 1, 2012. The PDUFA goal date was extended by three months after we requested and received additional immunogenicity data that required more time for review. This document summarizes the Division’s recommendations on the application.

On 5/9/14 the Applicant submitted a BTD request, based on greater BMD response and safety (less hypercalcemia) in abaloparatide-treated patients compared to Forteo. This request was denied, as these data were not considered to establish a clinically significant improvement over approved therapy.

On 5/22/15 the Applicant submitted a second BTD request, citing phase 3 fracture data in addition to the benefits claimed previously. DBRUP responded that there was statistical overlap in vertebral fracture risk reduction between abaloparatide and teriparatide in study 003, and also statistical overlap with zoledronic acid and denosumab fracture data in previous studies. Thus, this request was also denied.

In addition, you will conduct enhanced pharmacovigilance of osteosarcoma cases identified among all patients currently or previously treated with abaloparatide, regardless of formulation or indication of use. citations.quote: #3189-1 Enhanced Assessment of Immunogenicity in Patients Treated with Tymlos (abaloparatide)

Part 2: Test all confirmed anti-abaloparatide positive serum samples from patients enrolled in the BA058-05-003 study for antibodies able to cross-react with or neutralize endogenous parathyroid hormone (PTH) or parathyroid hormone related peptide (PTHrP).
